title: Self-adjointness of the low degree projection
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega_i$ be its outcome space. For every $k\in\mathbb N$ and functions $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $\mathbb E_P[(f^{\le k})g]=\mathbb E_P[f(g^{\le k})]$, where $f^{\le k}$ and $g^{\le k}$ denote the low degree projections and $\mathbb E_P$ is expectation under the product mass.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces
Every atom mass is strictly positive and each coordinate's masses sum to one
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P[f^{\le k}g]=\mathbb E_P[fg^{\le k}]$.
